title: Coherence and the local comparison with the graded section module on Proj
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}S_d$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring with $S_0$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $f_1,\ldots,f_r\in S_1$ generate $S$ as an $S_0$-algebra, with $r\ge0$. Let $M=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}M_n$ be a finitely generated $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] with $S_aM_b\subseteq M_{a+b}$. Put $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj] and $\mathcal F=\widetilde M$, using the associated module sheaf of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists]. For $n\in\mathbf Z$ put $M(n)_d=M_{n+d}$, $\mathcal O_X(n)=\widetilde{S(n)}$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], and $\mathcal F(n)=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(n)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $\alpha_{M,n}:\mathcal F(n)\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde{M(n)}$ be the canonical multiplication isomorphism of [lem-sfb-standard-proj-twist-tensor]. Equip $N=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\Gamma(X,\mathcal F(n))$ with the graded $S$-action defined by multiplication by the canonical sections of $\mathcal O_X(e)$ for $s\in S_e$, as in [lem-sfb-proj-section-module-reconstruction]. Define $\phi_n:M_n\to N_n$ by composing the section map $x\mapsto x/1$ with $\Gamma(\alpha_{M,n}^{-1})$. Then $S$ is Noetherian, $\mathcal F$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and $\phi=\bigoplus_n\phi_n:M\to N$ is a degree-preserving $S$-linear map. For each $i$, its induced map $\phi_{(f_i)}:M_{(f_i)}\to N_{(f_i)}$ on degree-zero fractions [def-sc-degree-zero-module-fractions] is an isomorphism. Its inverse, under $M_{(f_i)}=\Gamma(D_+(f_i),\mathcal F)$, is $t/f_i^a\mapsto t|_{D_+(f_i)}\otimes f_i^{-a}$ for $a\ge0$ and $t\in N_a$, where $f_i^{-a}$ is the inverse trivialization of $\mathcal O_X(a)$ on that chart. The assertions allow $r=0$, empty standard opens, negative generator degrees, and $M=0$.

proof.text: The map $S_0[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to S$, $T_j\mapsto f_j$, is surjective by the algebra-generation hypothesis. Thus $S$ is a finite type $S_0$-algebra, including when $r=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to the assumed Noetherian ring $S_0$ to conclude that $S$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence, first assertion; the Noetherian ring used in Tag 0AG7.

proof.text: Put $U_i=D_+(f_i)$ and $R_i=S_{(f_i)}$. For homogeneous $s\in S_d$ with $d>0$, express $s$ as a polynomial in the $f_j$ and take its degree-$d$ part. Every remaining monomial has a factor $f_j$, so $s\in(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. Conversely each $f_j$ lies in $S_+$, hence $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)=S_+$. The cover and affine-chart assertions of [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open] give $X=\bigcup_iU_i$ and $U_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_i$. Thus the degree-one charts cover. If $r=0$, the same positive-degree projection gives $S_+=0$ and the empty cover says $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 01M4, lemma-standard-open; Algebra Tag 00JP, lemma-topology-proj, affine charts and cover criterion.

proof.text: For each $i$, $R_i$ is generated as an $S_0$-algebra by the finitely many ratios $f_j/f_i$. Indeed, a degree-zero fraction has form $s/f_i^a$ with $a\ge0$ and $s\in S_a$. Write $s$ as a polynomial in the $f_j$ and take its degree-$a$ part in the direct sum grading. Every surviving monomial has total degree $a$, so division by $f_i^a$ expresses the fraction as the same polynomial in the ratios $f_j/f_i$. This also works in a zero localization ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] again to see that every $R_i$ is Noetherian. The affine cover of step 2 therefore makes $X$ locally Noetherian, in the sense of [pqf-def-locnoeth].

source.place: Tag 0AG7, opening coherence argument, expanded using Tag 00FN and the standard degree-one affine charts.

proof.text: Choose a finite generating family for $M$. Replace it by the union of the homogeneous components of its members; each member has finite support and is the sum of its components, so the resulting finite homogeneous family still generates $M$. Denote it by $m_1,\ldots,m_k$, with $m_j\in M_{d_j}$ and $d_j\in\mathbf Z$. For $M=0$ take the empty family.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, finite graded module in the first sentence of the proof; elementary homogeneous-generator selection.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and invert $f=f_i$. In $M_f$ put $q_j=f^{-d_j}m_j$, of degree zero. For $d_j\ge0$ this is $m_j/f^{d_j}$; for $d_j<0$ it is $f^{|d_j|}m_j/1$, so in either case it is an allowed degree-zero fraction. If $x/f^a\in M_{(f)}$ with $x\in M_a$, express $x=\sum_j s_jm_j$ and project to degree $a$ to take $s_j\in S_{a-d_j}$ (zero when $a-d_j<0$). Then $x/f^a=\sum_j(s_jf^{d_j-a})q_j$, with each coefficient of degree zero in $S_f$. More explicitly, when $a-d_j\ge0$ the coefficient is the allowed fraction $s_j/f^{a-d_j}$; when $a-d_j<0$ the coefficient is zero because $s_j=0$. Thus the $q_j$ generate $M_{(f)}$ over $S_{(f)}$. All powers with negative exponents here occur after $f$ has been inverted; no lower bound on the $d_j$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, first sentence: explicit finite-generation calculation for the associated sheaf on each degree-one chart.

proof.text: By clauses (b),(c) of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists], $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent and $\mathcal F(U_i)=M_{(f_i)}$. Step 5 and the affine finite-type criterion [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](c) make $\mathcal F$ of finite type. Step 3 supplies precisely the locally Noetherian hypothesis for [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; its equivalence now makes $\mathcal F$ coherent. On an empty $X$ the finite-type and coherence conditions are vacuous, so this argument includes $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AG7, first sentence; Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian, equivalence (1),(2); Properties Tag 01PB, lemma-finite-type-module.

proof.text:
The degree-one cover permits [lem-sfb-standard-proj-twist-tensor]. For $x\in M_n$, clause (d) of [lem-weil-pbc-proj-graded-module-sheaf-exists] applied to $M(n)$ gives its additive section $x/1$ of $\widetilde{M(n)}$. On $U_i$, multiplication defining $\alpha_{M,n}$ sends $(xf_i^{-n})\otimes f_i^n$ to $x/1$. Consequently $\phi_n(x)|_{U_i}=(xf_i^{-n})\otimes f_i^n$. This formula holds for every integer $n$: when $n<0$, write $b=-n>0$, so $xf_i^{-n}=f_i^b x/1\in M_{(f_i)}$ and $f_i^n=1/f_i^b\in S(n)_{(f_i)}$. These are allowed representatives under [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], and their product in $M(n)_{(f_i)}$ is $x/1$. For homogeneous $s\in S_e$, its canonical twist section on $U_i$ has coefficient $s/f_i^e$ in the basis $f_i^e$. The multiplication formula and associativity in the twist lemma therefore give
$$(s\phi_n(x))|_{U_i}=(sxf_i^{-(e+n)})\otimes f_i^{e+n}=\phi_{n+e}(sx)|_{U_i}.$$
Equality on the cover is equality of global sections. Additivity follows from the section map and the linear isomorphism $\alpha^{-1}$. Taking direct sums, and expanding arbitrary elements into their finitely many homogeneous components, proves that $\phi$ is a degree-preserving $S$-linear map for the action in the statement.

source.place: Tag 01MT, lemma-apply-modules, maps equation-map-global-sections-degree-n-simplified and equation-global-sections-more-generally-simplified; fraction multiplication defining the maps.

proof.text:
Fix $i$. Apply [lem-sfb-proj-section-module-reconstruction] to the quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ from step 6 and the given finite degree-one algebra generators. On $U_i$ its isomorphism has the section map
$$\psi_i:N_{(f_i)}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal F)=M_{(f_i)},\qquad t/f_i^a\mapsto t|_{U_i}\otimes f_i^{-a}.$$
The reconstruction node states both that this is an isomorphism and this exact chart formula; it requires no additional finiteness of $N$. The ordinary fraction relation is respected explicitly: if $x/f_i^a=y/f_i^b$, some $c\ge0$ has $f_i^c(f_i^b x-f_i^a y)=0$. Step 7 sends this equation to $f_i^c(f_i^b\phi_a(x)-f_i^a\phi_b(y))=0$, which identifies the image fractions. Thus the localized map $\phi_{(f_i)}$ sends $x/f_i^a$ to $\phi_a(x)/f_i^a$. Substitution of the formula in step 7 gives
$$\psi_i(\phi_{(f_i)}(x/f_i^a))=((xf_i^{-a})\otimes f_i^a)\otimes f_i^{-a}=x/f_i^a.$$
The cancellation uses the unital associative twist multiplication of [lem-sfb-standard-proj-twist-tensor]. Every degree-zero fraction has such a representative, so $\psi_i\phi_{(f_i)}=1$. Since $\psi_i$ is an isomorphism, $\phi_{(f_i)}=\psi_i^{-1}$, proving the required isomorphism and inverse formula. If $U_i$ is empty its section and fraction modules are zero and the same identities hold. Together with the empty-cover case and the empty generator family of step 4, this covers every edge case stated in the item.
